section_summary: This section closes an earlier copy of a roster of Japanese residents in Guatemala, then reproduces the State Department’s circulation memorandum, Guatemala despatch no. 2962, and its complete enclosure. The despatch explains that Chinese Consul General Tchou Che-tsien supplied dossiers on ten adult Japanese residents as intelligence concerning possible subversive activity. A separate Santiago despatch reports cooperation between the American Embassy and Chinese Chargé d’Affaires Dr. Dai on Japanese cases and subversive activities, followed by a Department of State circulation sheet.

subfiles.title: Names and General Information Concerning Japanese Presently Residing in the Republic of Guatemala, C.A. (conclusion of earlier copy)
subfiles.about: The page concludes an earlier copy of a biographical roster of adult Japanese residents in Guatemala.
subfiles.summary: Final page of the Guatemala roster of Japanese residents: an elderly carpenter and others, with occupations, residences and documentation; repeated on page 467.

subfiles.title: Department of State circulation memorandum for Guatemala despatch no. 2962
subfiles.to: Military Intelligence Division; Office of Naval Intelligence; Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.about: The Department circulates a copy of the Guatemala Legation’s despatch on Japanese subversive activities and its enclosure.
subfiles.summary: Memorandum circulates Despatch No. 2962 from Guatemala to military, naval and federal intelligence authorities.

subfiles.title: Despatch no. 2962: Japanese Subversive Activities
subfiles.from: Fay Allen DesPortes, American Legation at Guatemala
subfiles.about: The Legation forwards a Chinese-supplied dossier on adult Japanese residents of Guatemala and reports the remaining Japanese presence in El Salvador.
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 2962: the Chinese Consul General supplied a list of every known adult Japanese in Guatemala, disclosing ten people, at least seven more than suspected; the last two Japanese men in El Salvador were deported May 18.

subfiles.title: Names and General Information Concerning Japanese Presently Residing in Republic of Guatemala, C.A.
subfiles.about: The enclosure supplies personal dossiers on ten adult Japanese residents of Guatemala.
subfiles.summary: Translated Guatemala roster of Japanese residents with ages, occupations and addresses; two men detained in Police Barracks No. 1, others seamstresses, bakers, a butler and cooks.

subfiles.title: Despatch no. 3545: Cooperation with Chinese Legation in Santiago
subfiles.from: Claude G. Bowers, American Embassy at Santiago
subfiles.about: The Embassy reports Chinese diplomatic cooperation on Proclaimed List cases involving Japanese persons and on Japanese subversive activities.
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 3545: the Chinese Chargé Dr. Dai agreed to cooperate with the Embassy on Proclaimed List matters and was consulted on Japanese cases.

subfiles.title: Department of State circulation memorandum for Santiago despatch no. 3545
subfiles.to: Military Intelligence Division; Office of Naval Intelligence; Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.about: The Department circulates the Santiago despatch on cooperation with the Chinese Legation to American intelligence agencies.
subfiles.summary: Routing sheet circulates the strictly confidential Santiago despatch on cooperation with the Chinese Legation to intelligence offices.
